hints.title: Median Minimizes Absolute Deviations
hints.text: For any fixed group of values, the sum of absolute deviations to a chosen target is minimized when that target is chosen as the median.

hints.title: Sliding Window Analysis
hints.text: Examine contiguous windows of length k. For each window, compute the cost to equalize all elements to the window median.

hints.title: Tracking Window Order
hints.text: Sort the window or maintain an ordered structure to find the median and evaluate the sum of distances to each element in the window.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def minOperationsToEqualize(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        ans = float('inf')
        for i in range(n - k + 1):
            window = sorted(nums[i:i + k])
            med = window[k // 2]
            cost = sum(abs(x - med) for x in window)
            ans = min(ans, cost)
        return ans
```

complexity.notes: Can be optimized to O(n log k) using two balanced heaps or Fenwick trees.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating arbitrary target values without median logic requires testing every integer in the range.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Maintaining window elements in sorted order costs O(k) space and guarantees optimal median evaluation.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Expects understanding of median optimality for L1 distance minimization and sliding window techniques.
